summary.en: Ask whether the question word supplies the subject or the object.

body.en:
From season 1, episode 5.

The filming scene in episode 5 asks *Qu'est-ce qui se passe?*. The question concerns the thing that is happening. *qui* is part of a question about the subject of the following clause.

With *qu'est-ce que*, another subject normally follows, as when asking what a particular person does. The short endings are easy to blur in connected speech, so listen to the words after them too.

Do not decide that every *qui* must mean a person is being asked about. In this construction it signals the grammatical role of the question, and the answer need not be a person.

On replay, identify the following subject and verb. If there is no separate subject because the question asks what is happening, *qu'est-ce qui* is a pattern worth recognising as a whole rather than translating word by word.
